lines.trans: Runt, you will pay this expensive bill!
Chef, but this is very big money.
You will work for free a whole month!
Life is constantly putting us to the test.
Some people easily cope with difficulties.
And some people give up right away.
For some life is a kaleidoscope of adventures.
For others, a series of bitter disappointments.
Stop daydreaming, go wash the frying pans!
In any case one must be ready for everything.
Life teaches us unexpected turns of fate.
I will definitely deal with this problem.

Tomorrow new culinary victories await me!

lines.trans: Now that is the right attitude for a cook!
Tomorrow new culinary victories await me!
Tomorrow new culinary victories await me!

meanings.note: Coordinating or subordinating Russian conjunction meaning 'and', linking clauses in spoken dialogue.
Secondary conversational sense ('so, and what about') (starting a question: а жвачку?) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: And this is for you.
And where's the toy car?
Dad, did you bring any gum?

meanings.note: Privative prefix 'бес-' ('without, -less', before voiceless consonants) (stem 'платно'). Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.trans: If they're late, the pizza is free.
Children get in free.

examples.text: Если опоздают, пицца бесплатно. Может, закажем?
examples.trans: If they're late, the pizza is free. Maybe we should order?

meanings.note: Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('big, large').

examples.trans: A big city.
The sum is very large.

examples.text: Аракелян просит время. Сумма очень большая.
examples.trans: Arakelyan is asking for more time. The sum is very large.

meanings.note: the present tense is normally left out: я мэр = I am the mayor
Secondary conversational sense ('there is, there are') (present есть; у меня есть = I have) used in spoken Russian dialogue.
future: буду / будешь ... + infinitive

examples.trans: I have a toy car.
Childhood was hard.
You will be asking for forgiveness.

meanings.note: Russian preposition meaning 'in' that governs a specific oblique case on the following noun phrase.
Secondary conversational sense ('into, to') (+ accusative (where to)) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: How is it in Hungary?
I grew up in a communal flat.
Hello! How was it in Hungary?

meanings.note: Russian determiner/pronoun ('all') agreeing in gender, number, and case with the noun phrase it specifies.
Secondary conversational sense ('everything') (neuter всё) used in spoken Russian dialogue.
Secondary conversational sense ('everyone') (plural все) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: Everything's fine.
As you all know...
Share with everyone.

meanings.note: Conversational Russian particle ('here') that adds modal nuance, emphasis, or discourse tone in spoken dialogue.
Secondary conversational sense ('! = you'll see!') (emphasis) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: There, look.
Here's my toy car.
All right, here you go. There, look.

meanings.note: Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('bitter').

examples.trans: This is a bitter disappointment.
For others, a series of bitter disappointments.

meanings.note: usually the short form: я готов (m), я готова (f)

examples.trans: I'm ready!
Lunch is ready.
Right, I'm ready!

meanings.note: plural only: there is no singular in everyday use

examples.trans: I have no money.
The money is on the table.
Gum? I didn't have enough money.

meanings.note: Russian preposition meaning 'for' that governs a specific oblique case on the following noun phrase.

examples.trans: We could open a salon for you.
This is for you.

examples.text: Для вас можно открыть салон красоты.
examples.trans: We could open a beauty salon for you.

meanings.note: to a loved one, and at the start of letters
to a loved one, and at the start of letters

examples.trans: These are expensive clothes.
Darling, I'm home!

examples.text: В Москве вам дают деньги на дорогую одежду, а мозги не дают.
examples.trans: In Moscow they give you money for expensive clothes, but they don't give you brains.

meanings.note: Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('other, another, different').
Secondary conversational sense ('different') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: Could we go somewhere else?
That's a different building.

examples.text: Послушайте, а можно в другое место? Здесь плохо пахнет.
examples.trans: Listen, could we go somewhere else? It smells bad in here.

meanings.note: Russian imperfective verb expressing ongoing, habitual, or repeated action meaning 'to wait', forming an aspectual pair with 'подождать'; conjugates for person and number in the present/future and agrees in gender in the past tense.
Secondary conversational sense ('to expect') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: Don't wait for me.
I'm waiting for you.
So I shouldn't wait for you tonight?

meanings.note: Common feminine noun meaning 'life' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: That's life.
I want a different life.
Working. Making people's lives better.

meanings.note: Prefix 'за-' marks beginning an action, covering, or stopping by along the way (stem 'втра').

examples.trans: We'll arrange something for tomorrow.
See you tomorrow!

examples.text: Позвони мне вечером. Договоримся на завтра.
examples.trans: Call me this evening. We'll arrange something for tomorrow.

meanings.note: Russian imperfective verb expressing ongoing, habitual, or repeated action meaning 'to go', forming an aspectual pair with 'пойти'; conjugates for person and number in the present/future and agrees in gender in the past tense.
Secondary conversational sense ('expression') (to run for a second term) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: I'm going home.
He is running for a second term.

examples.text: Я очень люблю наш город. Поэтому я иду на второй срок.
examples.trans: I love our town very much. That's why I'm running for a second term.

meanings.note: Prefix 'ис-' ('out from within') marks extraction or exhaustion (stem 'пытывать'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to experience, feel', paired with 'испытать'.

examples.text: Аркадий Борисович испытывает к вам чувства.
examples.trans: Arkady Borisovich has feelings for you.
To experience joy.

examples.text: Жизнь постоянно испытывает нас на прочность.
examples.trans: Life is constantly putting us to the test.

meanings.note: Russian preposition meaning 'to' that governs a specific oblique case on the following noun phrase.

examples.trans: There's someone here to see you.
I'm going to Mum's.

examples.text: Аркадий Борисович, извините, тут к вам человек.
examples.trans: Arkady Borisovich, I'm sorry, there's a man here to see you.

meanings.en: kaleidoscope (optical device or succession of events)
meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'kaleidoscope' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: Life is a kaleidoscope of adventures.
For some life is a kaleidoscope of adventures.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian pronoun ('someone') whose case form reflects its grammatical role in the clause.

examples.trans: Finally someone is for the people!

examples.text: Слушай, тут пишут: «Гордость России! Наконец-то кто-то за народ!»
examples.trans: Listen, here they write: 'Pride of Russia! Finally someone is for the people!'

examples.text: Ты что, не понимаешь? Я задавить кого-то мог!
examples.trans: Don't you understand? I could have run someone over!

meanings.note: connected with cooking or the kitchen

examples.trans: He showed excellent culinary skills.

examples.text: Я отличный повар и закончил кулинарный колледж.
examples.trans: I am an excellent cook and finished culinary college.

examples.text: Ладно, сейчас проверим твои настоящие кулинарные навыки.
examples.trans: Fine, now we will test your real culinary skills.

meanings.note: Manner or predicative adverb in '-о' derived from the corresponding adjective stem, used in everyday speech to mean 'easily'.

examples.trans: Come on, it's easy.
It's easy for you to say.

examples.text: Да это легко. Схватил собачку в парке и побежал.
examples.trans: Come on, it's easy. Grab the little dog in the park and run.

meanings.note: Descriptive Russian adjective meaning 'any', agreeing in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies.

examples.trans: Any time.
Anyone knows that.

examples.text: Любая обезьяна эти выборы выиграет! Ты что, хуже обезьяны?
examples.trans: Any monkey will win this election! What, are you worse than a monkey?

meanings.note: Declinable masculine noun meaning 'month', changing its case ending across all six Russian grammatical cases to mark its role in the clause.

examples.trans: I've been living here for a month.
The election is in a month.

examples.text: Мы с Пашей вместе уже месяц.
examples.trans: Pasha and I have been together for a month now.

meanings.note: Russian imperfective verb expressing ongoing, habitual, or repeated action meaning 'to dream', forming an aspectual pair with 'помечтать'; conjugates for person and number in the present/future and agrees in gender in the past tense.
Secondary conversational sense ('dream on!') (imperative, sarcastic: мечтай!) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: I dream of the sea.

examples.text: Мечтай дальше, этот столик уже давно забронирован!
examples.trans: Dream on, that table has been booked for a long time already!

examples.text: С самого детства Макс мечтал стать знаменитым шеф-поваром.
examples.trans: Since childhood Max dreamed of becoming a famous head chef.

meanings.note: нас = us (gen/acc/prep); у нас = we have, at our place
Secondary conversational sense ('other forms:  (gen/acc),  (dat),  (instr),  (prep)') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: We've done a lot.
Our toilet is dirty.

examples.text: Смотрите, какой у нас грязный унитаз!
examples.trans: Look, how dirty our toilet is!

meanings.note: Russian imperfective verb expressing ongoing, habitual, or repeated action meaning 'to wash', forming an aspectual pair with 'помыть'; conjugates for person and number in the present/future and agrees in gender in the past tense.

examples.text: Юля, встала и пошла мыть посуду!
examples.trans: Yulia, get up and go wash the dishes!
Wash your hands before eating.

examples.text: Пока ещё на мои деньги куплен! Встала и мыть посуду, шагом марш!
examples.trans: It's still bought with my money! Get up and wash the dishes, forward march!

meanings.note: Russian preposition meaning 'on' that governs a specific oblique case on the following noun phrase.
Secondary conversational sense ('onto, to; for') (+ accusative: на второй срок) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: The programme is on the website.
He is running for a second term.

examples.text: Я очень люблю наш город. Поэтому я иду на второй срок.
examples.trans: I love our town very much. That's why I'm running for a second term.

meanings.en: must, need to, it is necessary
meanings.note: Manner or predicative adverb in '-о' derived from the corresponding adjective stem, used in everyday speech to mean 'it is necessary'.

examples.trans: It needs a wash.
We need to do even more.
It needs a wash!

meanings.note: Prefix 'на-' marks surface contact, accumulation, or completing a quantity (stem 'строй'). Common masculine noun meaning 'attitude, mood, spirit' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: The cook has the right attitude.

examples.text: Вот это правильный настрой для повара!
examples.trans: Now that is the right attitude for a cook!
Now that is a great attitude, chef!

meanings.note: Negative prefix 'не-' ('un-, non-, not') (stem 'ожиданный'). Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('unexpected, sudden').

examples.trans: It was an unexpected turn.

examples.text: Жизнь учит нас неожиданным поворотам судьбы.
examples.trans: Life teaches us unexpected turns of fate.

examples.text: Самоуверенность часто приводит к неожиданным проблемам.
examples.trans: Overconfidence often leads to unexpected problems.

meanings.note: Coordinating or subordinating Russian conjunction meaning 'but', linking clauses in spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Мы сделали много, но надо ещё.
examples.trans: We've done a lot, but we need more.
I want to, but I can't.

examples.text: Мы сделали много, но надо сделать ещё больше.
examples.trans: We've done a lot, but we need to do even more.

meanings.note: Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('new').

examples.trans: A new house.
I need a new job.

examples.text: Ну что, довольна? Теперь новую работу искать.
examples.trans: Well, happy now? Now I have to look for a new job.

meanings.note: Manner or predicative adverb in '-о' derived from the corresponding adjective stem, used in everyday speech to mean 'definitely'.

examples.trans: I'll definitely buy you a tank.

examples.text: Государство обязательно увидит и назначит операцию.
examples.trans: The state will surely see and will schedule the surgery.
I will definitely come tomorrow.

meanings.note: playful derogatory nickname used by Chef Barinov for Max

examples.trans: Runt, are you still standing here?
The chef often called the newcomer a runt.

examples.text: Огузок, ты официально принят в штат нашего ресторана!
examples.trans: Rump, you are officially hired onto our restaurant staff!

meanings.note: agrees in gender and case with the noun
Secondary conversational sense ('alone') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: Give me just one.
I have one brother.

examples.text: У тебя же есть ещё. Дай хоть одну.
examples.trans: But you've still got some. Give me just one.

meanings.en: to pay for, to pay off (+ accusative)
meanings.note: Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to pay, to pay off', paired with 'оплачивать'.

examples.text: Послушай, я оплачу весь долг этой женщины!
examples.trans: Listen, I'll pay this woman's entire debt!

examples.text: Он уже оплатил счёт в ресторане.
examples.trans: He has already paid the bill at the restaurant.

examples.text: Послушай, я оплачу весь долг этой женщины! Клянусь, весь долг!
examples.trans: Listen, I'll pay this woman's entire debt! I swear, the whole debt!

meanings.note: Russian imperfective verb expressing ongoing, habitual, or repeated action meaning 'to lower', forming an aspectual pair with 'опустить'; conjugates for person and number in the present/future and agrees in gender in the past tense.

examples.trans: Lower him straight into the water.
He puts his hands into his pockets.

examples.text: Давай, опускайте его прямо в воду!
examples.trans: Go on, lower him straight into the water!

meanings.note: Invariable Russian adverb used to modify verbs or whole clauses with the sense 'very'.
Secondary conversational sense ('very much') (with verbs: очень люблю) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: I love our town very much.
It's very hard.

examples.text: Я очень люблю наш город. Поэтому я иду на второй срок.
examples.trans: I love our town very much. That's why I'm running for a second term.

meanings.note: Declinable feminine noun meaning 'victory', changing its case ending across all six Russian grammatical cases to mark its role in the clause.

examples.trans: People applaud your victory!
The day of great Victory.

examples.text: Люди в городе аплодируют вашей победе!
examples.trans: People in the town are applauding your victory!

meanings.note: Declinable masculine noun meaning 'cook', changing its case ending across all six Russian grammatical cases to mark its role in the clause.

examples.trans: There is this English chef.

examples.text: Есть такой английский повар. Я по его передачам научусь готовить.
examples.trans: There is this English chef. I will learn to cook from his shows.

examples.text: Я хочу работать поваром в ресторане.
examples.trans: I want to work as a cook in a restaurant.

meanings.note: Declinable masculine noun meaning 'turn', changing its case ending across all six Russian grammatical cases to mark its role in the clause.

examples.trans: The car slowed down before the bend.
The forest began beyond the turn.
You better slow down before the turn!

meanings.note: Manner or predicative adverb in '-о' derived from the corresponding adjective stem, used in everyday speech to mean 'constantly'.

examples.trans: What are you constantly afraid of?
He was constantly late for work.
What are you constantly afraid of, Kostik?

meanings.note: Qualitative or relational adjective formed with the productive '-н-' suffix, meaning 'correct' and agreeing in gender, number, and case.

examples.trans: A course of the correct antibiotics.
That is the correct answer.
We have prescribed a course of the correct antibiotics.

meanings.note: Verbal action or result neuter noun formed with '-ение'/'-ание', meaning 'adventure' in conversational and formal Russian.

examples.trans: The main adventure is only just beginning!

examples.text: В Москве Макса ждали новые приключения.
examples.trans: New adventures awaited Max in Moscow.

examples.text: И главное приключение ещё только начинается!
examples.trans: And the main adventure is only just beginning!

meanings.note: 'будут проблемы' = there'll be trouble

examples.trans: That's not a problem.
I have a problem.
I know the problems of ordinary people.

meanings.note: испытывать на прочность = to test one's strength

examples.trans: Life puts us to the test.

examples.text: Жизнь постоянно испытывает нас на прочность.
examples.trans: Life is constantly putting us to the test.

meanings.note: работать + instrumental = to work as: работать мэром

examples.trans: I work as mayor.
Where do you work?

examples.text: Я уже четыре года работаю мэром.
examples.trans: I've been working as mayor for four years now.

meanings.note: Prefix 'раз-' ('apart, un-, thoroughly') indicates distribution or intensive action (stem 'очарование'). Verbal action/result neuter noun formed with '-ение'/'-ание'. Common neuter noun meaning 'disappointment' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: It was a bitter disappointment.
For others, a series of bitter disappointments.

meanings.note: Derived feminine noun formed with a productive Slavic suffix, used in spoken Russian to mean 'hand'.

examples.trans: Give me your hand.
I shake your hand! (a goodbye)
Right, cheers then.

meanings.note: + instrumental; со before some consonant clusters: со всеми

examples.trans: Share with everyone.
I'm with Dad.
Share it all equally with everyone, understand?

meanings.note: pan with a handle used for frying food

examples.trans: A heavy frying pan was sizzling on the stove.

examples.text: Он быстро снял сковородку с огня.
examples.trans: He quickly took the frying pan off the heat.

examples.text: Во имя тяжёлой сковородки и половника!
examples.trans: In the name of the heavy frying pan and ladle!

meanings.note: Declinable masculine noun meaning 'case', changing its case ending across all six Russian grammatical cases to mark its role in the clause.
Secondary conversational sense ('incident') used in spoken Russian dialogue.
Secondary conversational sense ('chance') (на всякий случай = just in case) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: Take it, just in case.
This is a strange case.

examples.text: Возьмите, пожалуйста. На случай, если передумаете.
examples.trans: Please take this. In case you change your mind.

справиться.gloss: to manage, to cope, to handle

meanings.note: often + с + instrumental, or used absolutely

examples.text: Мы за два года тут не справимся.
examples.trans: We won't manage here in two years.

examples.text: Конечно, не справитесь. Вы же не я.
examples.trans: Of course you won't manage. You're not me, after all.

examples.text: Мы обязательно справимся и с этим.
examples.trans: We will definitely cope with this too.

meanings.note: imperfective, governs с + instrumental

examples.text: Он легко справлялся с любой задачей.
examples.trans: He easily coped with any task.
Do not argue, Fedya managed somehow!

examples.text: Ты отлично справляешься сегодня на смене.
examples.trans: You are doing great on the shift today.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'разу').

examples.trans: You can see it at once.
I understood at once.
Now there's a businesswoman, you can see it at once.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'удьба'). Common feminine noun meaning 'fate, destiny, fortune' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: The people are interested in his fate.
Such is my fate.
And the people are interested in his fate.

meanings.note: Declinable masculine noun meaning 'account', changing its case ending across all six Russian grammatical cases to mark its role in the clause.
Secondary conversational sense ('bill, check') (in a restaurant) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: Or a bank account.
Bring the bill, please.

examples.text: Или счёт в банке. Потому что они все обманщики.
examples.trans: Or a bank account. Because they are all cheats.

meanings.note: Abstract feminine noun formed with the Slavic suffix '-ость' ('-ness, -ity') from the corresponding adjective. Common feminine noun meaning 'difficulty, hardship' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: He easily copes with difficulties.
Some people easily cope with difficulties.

examples.text: Настоящий мастер никогда не боится трудностей.
examples.trans: A true master is never afraid of difficulties.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian pronoun ('you') whose case form reflects its grammatical role in the clause.
Secondary conversational sense ('other forms:  (gen/acc),  (dat),  (instr),  (prep)') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: You're greedy!
Have you got any more?
Dad, did you bring any gum?

meanings.note: Prefix 'у-' marks departure, removal, or successful completion (stem 'чить'). Used in Russian as an imperfective verb expressing ongoing, habitual, or repeated action meaning 'to learn', forming an aspectual pair with 'выучить'.
Secondary conversational sense ('to teach') (+ accusative of the person) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: I'm doing my homework.
We're learning Russian.
Not allowed? All right, I'll go and do my homework.

meanings.note: impersonal, + genitive: денег не хватило = there wasn't enough money
Secondary conversational sense ('that's enough!') (хватит!) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: There wasn't enough money.
Gum? I didn't have enough money.

examples.text: Хватит спорить из-за пустяков, давайте лучше спокойно работать!
examples.trans: Enough arguing over trifles, let us just work calmly instead!

meanings.note: Descriptive Russian adjective meaning 'whole', agreeing in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies.
Secondary conversational sense ('intact, in one piece') (not broken) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Я не могу гулять здесь целый день.
examples.trans: I can't walk around here all day.
We waited for a whole hour.

examples.text: Илья Олегович! Я не могу гулять здесь целый день.
examples.trans: Ilya Olegovich! I can't walk around here all day.

meanings.note: Common feminine noun meaning 'series, succession' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: Life is a series of events.
For others, a series of bitter disappointments.

meanings.note: Borrowed from French 'chef' (head, leader, from Latin 'caput'); in Russian kitchen culture 'шеф' is the standard form of address for the executive head chef.

examples.trans: Cleverly thought out, boss!
The boss signed the order.
The chef is in the kitchen.

meanings.note: pointing at a thing or a situation; 'это' + noun = 'this is ...'
points at something: это моё = that's mine
Secondary conversational sense ('is') (linking word: главное — это народ) used in spoken Russian dialogue.
Secondary conversational sense ('other forms:') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: That's mine.
And this is for you.
And this is for you. A toy car!

meanings.note: alone: 'я этого не хочу' = I don't want that

examples.trans: This house.
I'm sick of this communal flat.

examples.text: Меня уже тошнит от этой коммуналки! У нас труба уже неделю течёт.
examples.trans: I'm sick of this communal flat! Our pipe has been leaking for a week now.

meanings.note: меня = me (genitive/accusative), мне = to me (dative)
Secondary conversational sense ('other forms:  (gen/acc),  (dat),  (instr),  (prep)') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: I'm doing my homework.
I grew up here.
Chef, I didn't take it.
